en: Minjab ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi, Sahl ibn 'Uthman, 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Zurarah al-Hadrami, Suwayd ibn Sa'id, and al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to us—Sahl and Minjab said: informed us, and the others said: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us—from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abdullah, who said: When this verse was revealed: "There is no sin upon those who believe and do righteous deeds regarding what they have tasted when they are conscious of Allah and believe..." to the end of the verse, the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to me: "It was said to me: You are of them."

Ubayd ibn Ya'ish and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani both narrated to us—they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is his—my father narrated to us, Abu Hayyan al-Taymi Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to Bilal at the dawn prayer: "O Bilal, tell me of the deed you have done in Islam that brings the most hope of benefit, for tonight I heard the rustling of your sandals before me in Paradise." Bilal said: "I have not done any deed in Islam that brings more hope of benefit to me than whenever I perform complete purification at any hour of the night or day, I pray with that purification whatever Allah has decreed for me to pray."

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Faraj narrated to me, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salamah informed me, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir informed us, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "I was shown Paradise and I saw the wife of Abu Talhah, then I heard a rustling ahead of me and behold, it was Bilal."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Bishr—meaning Ibn al-Sari—narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (pbuh), who said: "I entered Paradise and heard a footstep, so I said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'This is al-Ghumaysa' bint Milhan, the mother of Anas ibn Malik.'"

Hasan al-Hulwani narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah, from Anas, who said: The Prophet (pbuh) did not enter upon any woman except his wives, other than Umm Sulaym, for he used to enter upon her. When he was questioned about that, he said: "I have pity on her; her brother was killed with me."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Asim al-Kilabi informed me, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to 'Umar after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh): "Let us go to Umm Ayman to visit her, just as the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) used to visit her." When we reached her, she wept, so they said to her: "What makes you weep? What is with Allah is better for His Messenger (pbuh)." She said: "I am not weeping because I do not know that what is with Allah is better for His Messenger (pbuh), but rather I am weeping because the revelation has ceased from heaven." This moved them both to tears, so they began weeping with her.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) went to Umm Ayman and I went with him. She handed him a vessel containing a drink—he said—and I do not know whether she found him fasting or he did not desire it, so she began making clamor at him and scolding him.

Mahmud ibn Ghaylan Abu Ahmad narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Sinani narrated to us, Talhah ibn Yahya ibn Talhah informed us, from 'A'ishah bint Talhah, from 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "The quickest of you to join me will be the one with the longest hands." She said: So they used to measure against each other whose hand was the longest. She said: And Zaynab was the one among us with the longest hands, because she used to work with her hands and give in charity.

Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Qaysi both narrated to me from al-Mu'tamir—Ibn Hammad said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us—he said: I heard my father: Abu 'Uthman narrated to us, from Salman, who said: "Do not, if you are able, be the first to enter the market or the last to leave it, for it is the battleground of Satan and in it he sets up his banner." He said: And I was informed that Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet of Allah (pbuh) while Umm Salamah was with him. He said: He began speaking, then he departed. The Prophet of Allah (pbuh) said to Umm Salamah: "Who was this?"—or as he said. She said: "This was Dihyah." He said: Umm Salamah said: "By Allah, I thought he was none other than him until I heard the address of the Prophet of Allah (pbuh) relating our news"—or as he said. He said: I said to Abu 'Uthman, "From whom did you hear this?" He said, "From Usamah ibn Zayd."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, and 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Zakariyya'; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Zakariyya' narrated to us, from Firas, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: The wives of the Prophet (pbuh) gathered together, not a single woman among them remaining behind. Then Fatimah came walking as if her gait were the gait of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). He said: "Welcome, my daughter." Then he seated her on his right or on his left. Then he confided some words to her, and Fatimah wept. Then he whispered to her again, and she laughed. I said to her: "What makes you weep?" She said: "I am not one to disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)." I said: "I have never seen joy closer to grief than today." When she wept, I said to her: "Did the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) single you out with his words rather than us, and then you weep?" And I asked her what he had said, but she said: "I am not one to disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)." When he passed away, I asked her, and she said: "He had told me: 'Gabriel used to rehearse the Quran with me once every year, and he has rehearsed it with me twice this year, and I do not see it except that my appointed time has come; and indeed you are the first of my family to join me, and what an excellent predecessor I am for you.' So I wept at that. Then he whispered to me and said: 'Are you not pleased to be the chief of the women of the believers, or the chief of the women of this nation?' So I laughed at that."

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari, Fudayl ibn Husayn, narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Firas, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: The wives of the Prophet (pbuh) were with him, not a single one of them remaining behind, when Fatimah approached walking, her gait not deviating from the gait of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) in the least. When he saw her, he welcomed her and said: "Welcome, my daughter." Then he seated her on his right or on his left, then whispered to her, and she wept bitterly. When he saw her grief, he whispered to her a second time, and she laughed. So I said to her: "The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) singled you out among his wives for a secret, and then you weep?" When the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) stood up, I asked her: "What did the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) say to you?" She said: "I am not one to divulge the secret of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)." She said: When the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) passed away, I said: "I adjure you by the right I have over you that you tell me what the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to you." She said: "As for now, yes. As for when he whispered to me the first time, he informed me: 'Gabriel used to review the Quran with him once or twice every year, and he has reviewed it with him now twice, and I do not see the appointed time except that it has drawn near, so fear Allah and be patient, for what an excellent predecessor I am for you.'" She said: "So I wept the weeping you saw. When he saw my grief, he whispered to me a second time and said: 'O Fatimah, are you not pleased to be the chief of the women of the believers, or the chief of the women of this nation?'" She said: "So I laughed the laughter you saw."

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us, Ibrahim—meaning Ibn Sa'd—narrated to us, from his father, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me—and the wording is his—Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his father, that 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to him that 'A'ishah narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) called his daughter Fatimah and whispered to her, and she wept; then he whispered to her, and she laughed. 'A'ishah said: So I said to Fatimah, "What was this that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) whispered to you, so that you wept, then he whispered to you and you laughed?" She said: "He whispered to me and informed me of his death, so I wept; then he whispered to me and informed me that I would be the first of his household to follow him, so I laughed."

Abu Ma'n al-Raqashi narrated it to me, Wahb—meaning Ibn Jarir—narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard al-Nu'man—meaning Ibn Rashid—narrating from al-Zuhri, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, 'Ali ibn Husayn informed me that al-Miswar ibn Makhramah informed him that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib proposed to the daughter of Abu Jahl while Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), was his wife. When Fatimah heard of that, she came to the Prophet (pbuh) and said to him: "Your people are saying that you do not become angry for your daughters, and here is 'Ali about to marry the daughter of Abu Jahl." Al-Miswar said: So the Prophet (pbuh) stood up, and I heard him when he bore witness, then he said: "To proceed: I married Abu al-'As ibn al-Rabi', and he spoke to me and was truthful to me. And Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, is a piece of me, and I only dislike that they cause her distress. By Allah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah and the daughter of the enemy of Allah shall never be joined together with one man." He said: So 'Ali abandoned the proposal.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to me, Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim informed us, my father narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Halhalah al-Du'ali narrated to me, that Ibn Shihab narrated to him that 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to him that when they arrived in Medina from Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah after the slaying of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both), al-Miswar ibn Makhramah met him and said to him: "Do you have any need with me that you would command me with?" He said: I said to him, "No." He said to him: "Will you give me the sword of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)? For I fear that the people will overpower you for it; and by Allah, if you give it to me, it will never be reached until my soul departs. Indeed, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib sought to marry the daughter of Abu Jahl in addition to Fatimah, and I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) while he was delivering a sermon to the people regarding that upon this pulpit of his, while I was an adolescent on that day, and he said: 'Indeed Fatimah is of me, and I fear that she may be tempted regarding her religion.'" He said: Then he mentioned a son-in-law of his from Banu 'Abd Shams and praised his son-in-law relationship with him, speaking well of him. He said: "He spoke to me and was truthful to me, and he promised me and fulfilled his promise to me. And I do not make lawful that which is unlawful, nor do I make unlawful that which is lawful, but by Allah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah and the daughter of the enemy of Allah shall never be joined together in one place."

Abu Ma'mar Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hudhali narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Fatimah is only a piece of me; whatever hurts her hurts me."

Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yunus and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id both narrated to us from al-Layth ibn Sa'd—Ibn Yunus said: Layth narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Mulaykah al-Qurashi al-Taymi narrated to us that he heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) upon the pulpit saying: "Banu Hisham ibn al-Mughirah have asked my permission to marry their daughter to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. But I do not permit them, then I do not permit them, then I do not permit them—unless the son of Abu Talib wishes to divorce my daughter and marry their daughter. For my daughter is only a piece of me; what disquiets her disquiets me, and what hurts her hurts me."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated it to me, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, with this chain of narration, except that he said: "'Ayaya' Tabaqa'" without doubting; and he said: "infrequently driven to pasture"; and he said: "slender of waist, the best of her women, and the honor of her neighbor"; and he said: "and she does not scatter our provisions carelessly"; and he said: "and he gave me from every pair of slaughter animals a pair."
